name: Finn
lede: Finn is a deep purple whose name has no documented origin in our sources; it is a color we can measure but cannot yet explain.

sections.title: No story found
sections.body: The 29 books we searched do not discuss this name as a color [1]. The one match is an author's name in a bibliography, which is a person, not a color [1]. Our library traces the name only to a Wikipedia list, with no date [2]. Without a documented story, we describe the swatch and nothing more: its hex value is #683068, a deep purple with a slightly reddish cast [2].

sections.title: What can be measured
sections.body: Measured against the ISCC-NBS categories, the swatch is nearest to deep purple, 4.4 units of ΔE2000 away [2]. Its closest relatives by name are [[purple]], [[plum]] and [[dark-purple]], and the pale end of the family is [[dusty-purple]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of about 23,800 matches this color within the threshold, as photographed [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [3].
